answer: The basalt multiplier is published, charged in vertex, and plume lists each payment. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, since the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 8 for every identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 2037 identities would post 858 proofs and burn roughly 67 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
